function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common tools and platforms you can use to book flights, ranging from airline‑direct options to third‑party aggregators and even API services if you’re building your own solution. | Category | Tool / Platform | What It Offers | Typical Use Case | |----------|-----------------|----------------|------------------| | **Airline Direct** |
  • American Airlines (AA.com)
  • Delta Air Lines (Delta.com)
  • United Airlines (United.com)
  • Southwest Airlines (Southwest.com)
  • British Airways (BA.com)
  • Air France (AirFrance.com)
| Book directly with the carrier, often the cheapest fare, best for loyalty points, and direct customer support. | When you want to earn frequent flyer miles or have a specific airline preference. | | **Global Distribution Systems (GDS)** |
  • Amadeus
  • Sabre
  • Travelport (Apollo, Galileo, Worldspan)
| Professional travel agents use these systems to access a wide range of airlines, hotels, car rentals, etc. | For travel agencies or corporate travel departments needing bulk bookings or complex itineraries. | | **Online Travel Agencies (OTAs)** |
  • Expedia (Expedia.com)
  • Booking.com (Booking.com)
  • Hotels.com (Hotels.com)
  • Priceline (Priceline.com)
  • Orbitz (Orbitz.com)
| Aggregates flights, hotels, car rentals, and packages. Often offers bundle discounts. | For consumers looking for a one‑stop shop for all travel needs. | | **Metasearch Engines** |
  • Google Flights (Google.com/flights)
  • Kayak (Kayak.com)
  • Skyscanner (Skyscanner.com)
  • Momondo (Momondo.com)
| Search multiple airlines and OTAs simultaneously, compare prices, and see price trends. | For price comparison and finding the best deal across many sources. | | **Low‑Cost Carrier Sites** |
  • Ryanair (Ryanair.com)
  • EasyJet (EasyJet.com)
  • Norwegian Air (Norwegian.com)
  • JetBlue (JetBlue.com)
| Direct booking with budget airlines, often cheaper but with extra fees for baggage, seat selection, etc. | For travelers who prioritize low base fares and are willing to pay for extras separately. | | **Mobile Apps** |
  • Airbnb (for flights via partner airlines)
  • TripIt (for itinerary management)
  • Google Trips (now integrated into Google Travel)
| Convenient booking and itinerary tracking on the go. | For travelers who prefer mobile-first experiences. | | **API Services** |
  • Skyscanner API
  • Google Flights API (via Google Travel API)
  • FlightAware API
  • OpenSky API
| Allows developers to integrate flight search, booking, and real‑time flight status into their own apps or websites. | For businesses building custom travel solutions or integrating flight data into existing services. | | **Corporate Travel Platforms** |
  • Concur (SAP Concur)
  • Egencia (Expedia Group)
  • TravelPerk (TravelPerk.com)
| Handles corporate travel policies, expense reporting, and bulk booking. | For companies managing employee travel and ensuring compliance with corporate policies. | | **Specialty Platforms** |
  • Airbnb Experiences (for unique travel experiences)
  • Airbnb for Work (corporate travel solutions)
| Offers curated travel experiences and corporate travel solutions beyond just flights. | For travelers seeking unique experiences or corporate travel solutions that go beyond standard flight booking. | ### How to Choose the Right Tool 1. **Price vs. Service** – Low‑cost carriers offer cheap base fares but charge extra for baggage, seat selection, etc. OTAs and metasearch engines can help you compare those costs. 2. **Loyalty Programs** – If you’re a frequent flyer, booking directly with the airline might earn you more miles or points. 3. **Travel Complexity** – For multi‑city itineraries or group bookings, GDS or corporate platforms can handle complex routing and pricing. 4. **Convenience** – Mobile apps and metasearch engines are great for quick searches and booking on the go. 5. **Developer Needs** – If you’re building an app or website, consider using flight APIs to pull real‑time data and booking capabilities. Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper details on any specific platform or if you’re looking for a recommendation based on your travel preferences!
